To: Operations and Finance Leadership
From: Supply Chain Director
Subject: Network shipping plan to meet demand at lowest cost
Date: Today

Situation:
Our distribution network relies on multiple source locations to fulfill orders across a broad set of destination locations. Each source has limited available inventory and capacity, and each destination has a firm quantity requirement. Shipping costs vary by lane and carrier. Partial shipments are allowed, so orders can be split across multiple sources and routes when beneficial.

Problem:
We need a lane-level shipping plan that assigns quantities from each source to each destination in a way that:
- Does not exceed available inventory or capacity at any source
- Meets the full required quantities at every destination
- Minimizes total transportation spend across all lanes

This plan directly impacts customer service and cost performance. A well-structured allocation will reduce freight spend, avoid stockouts, and improve on-time fulfillment without overloading any single location.

Approach:
- Use the attached shipping data to evaluate viable routes and assign quantities that achieve the lowest landed cost while meeting all requirements.
- Allow split deliveries where cost-effective, leveraging partial shipments to balance capacity and demand across the network.
- Flag any imbalances (e.g., sources with insufficient inventory or destinations with unmet demand) and propose alternatives such as re-sourcing, transfers within the network, or temporary routing adjustments.
- Coordinate with transportation, warehouse operations, and customer service to confirm feasibility and timing before execution.

Next Steps:
Once the analysis is complete, we will circulate the recommended lane-level plan, identify savings opportunities, and document any required operational adjustments. We will also review sensitivity to changes in demand or rates and set up a cadence to refresh the plan as conditions evolve.
